sections.name: File setup (part 1)
sections.title: Panels, run records and evidence styles
sections.what: Sets sizes, spacing, borders and colours for the evidence drawer, citation dialog, fact blocks, run record details, snapshot tables, demo scope and portfolio panels. Many rules set a minimum height of 44 pixels so buttons and links are easy to tap.
sections.why: Likely reason: 44 pixels is a common minimum size for tappable items. The file does not state its reason.
sections.watch_out: Rules match class names and test IDs set in components, so renaming one there silently removes its styling.

sections.name: File setup (part 2)
sections.title: Yard home, industries and workspace styles
sections.what: Styles the yard hero heading and tagline, section headings, industry tiles and statistics, the opportunity panel, run links and a few workspace buttons.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code.
sections.watch_out: Several workspace rules match test IDs such as link-run and button-rekick, so changing those labels changes how the buttons look.

sections.name: @media (max-width: 767px)
sections.title: Phone layout rules
sections.what: On screens 767 pixels wide or less, stacks several multi-column layouts into one column and reduces padding in panels, dialogs and filters.
sections.why: Likely reason: keeps content readable on narrow screens.
sections.watch_out: The 767 pixel breakpoint is a fixed number. Check it against other breakpoints in the project before changing it.

summary: Stylesheet that adjusts the size, spacing and layout of the analysis screens (evidence panels, run records, portfolio tables and the yard home page), and deliberately leaves slide canvases and exported decks alone.
purpose: Keeps the look of the capital projects working screens in one place, separate from the shared design.
why: Likely reason: these screens need extra rules beyond the shared design, and the file header says slides and exported decks must not change. The reason is otherwise not stated in the code.
how: The browser loads these rules with the app. Each rule picks elements by class name or test ID and sets their size, spacing, colour or layout. Rules inside the media query at the end apply only on screens 767 pixels wide or less.
inputs: Class names and test IDs set by the screen components, plus colour and font values (CSS variables) defined elsewhere in the project.
outputs: Visual layout only. No data is read or saved.
risks: Rules depend on class names and test IDs set in other files, so a rename there silently removes styling. Colour variables are defined outside this file, so the final colours cannot be fully checked here.
debug: Open the screen in the browser's developer tools, select the element, and check which rule applies and whether the matching class name is present. If a layout breaks only on phones, check the media query at the end of the file.
